profile.size: Can reach about 3 feet and 15-18 lb, though fish over 10 lb are uncommon. FWC reports typical Florida catches averaging roughly 3-5 lb.
profile.diet: Feeds primarily on benthic invertebrates including shrimp, crabs and other small crustaceans found in seagrass and sand-flat sediments.
profile.behavior: Shallow-water flats specialist, often in less than one foot of water over seagrass and sometimes white sand. Small schools move across grass and sand flats searching for shrimp, crabs and other invertebrates. Fish are wary and rely on speed and a deeply forked tail. Northern Florida Keys telemetry also documents use of deeper channels that may provide refuge; this does not locate fish in real time.
profile.life_history: Matures at approximately 3-4 years and 17-18 inches total length; can live more than 23 years. Spawning occurs offshore, with seasonal movements between home ranges and spawning sites documented in some regional populations. Bahamas migration findings should not automatically be transferred to South Florida.
profile.spawning: Some Bahamas studies document spawning-site linkages and seasonal movements, but those findings should not be assumed for South Florida. FWC reports spawning from November through May, probably in deep or offshore water; the timing and routes of individual South Florida spawning migrations remain incompletely understood.
profile.overwintering: No South Florida overwintering route or seasonal refuge rule is encoded in this pilot profile.

factors.value_notes: Adult Bonefish thermal studies in the Bahamas measured performance optima around 26.7–28.0 °C and critical thermal limits. These are useful species-specific physiological findings, but they are not a validated South Florida habitat-preference curve and do not validate the configured 20–35 °C range or 25–31 °C ideal. Retained as provisional screening values only; independent local validation is still required.

regulations.summary: Florida bonefish are a catch-and-release-only fishery. Harvest is prohibited; temporary possession at the capture site for photography, measuring and weighing is allowed under FWC handling rules.
regulations.min_size: No harvest size limit because harvest is prohibited
regulations.max_size: No harvest size limit because harvest is prohibited
regulations.bag_limit: Catch-and-release only; no harvest bag limit
regulations.jurisdiction: Florida bonefish management rules extend into adjacent federal waters
regulations.source_name: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
regulations.notes: Harvest is prohibited. Multiple hooks used with live or dead natural bait to harvest or attempt harvest are prohibited. Temporary possession of one fish at a time for photography, measuring and weighing is allowed at the site of capture. Handle carefully and release promptly.

contexts.notes: Northern Florida Keys telemetry supports use of shallow foraging areas. Transfer to individual Biscayne Bay flats and mapped habitat classes requires local validation.
The cited telemetry documents use of deeper channels that may provide thermal refuge. Do not treat this as a validated South Florida channel preference or a real-time location claim.
